items.title: Clay Jenkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 18, 2016
items.q: The other trumpet teacher there is one of the — the classical trumpet teacher there, the main guy, is one of the best trumpet players I’ve ever heard in my life. His name is Jim Thompson.

ctx.x: Do the jazz students at Eastman, even the faculty, do you feel like more of a clannish clique at Eastman? Are you separate from the classical world or not?

No. I’m going to say that’s one thing I love about Eastman is generally speaking no. The other trumpet teacher there is one of the — the classical trumpet teacher there, the main guy, is one of the best trumpet players I’ve ever heard in my life. His name is Jim Thompson. He is so respectful of the jazz. Now that’s not always the case in schools. But Jim is so respectful to me and of the jazz thing. And he’s not a jazz player whatsoever. So I think in some schools it is an issue. It definitely is. Like oh you…
So some players do both. © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
